- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast to reflect downward risk or mean reversion bias.
- Model frequently overshoots after strong upward sentiment spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction or dampen peak forecasts.
- In early horizon (e.g., 30d) forecasts, model shows persistent bias toward higher prices; apply downward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model tends to misalign with true mean reversion; use sentiment-weighted smoothing or adjust for momentum decay.
- When true outcome shows sharp downward correction after high forecast, model may have overreacted to sentiment; reduce forecast slope or add downward buffer.
